seoDescription: Learn the essential steps to install Ruby on Rails on a Windows 10 machine. This comprehensive guide walks through setting up all necessary dependencies, including Node.js, Yarn, and SQLite3, ensuring a smooth development environment. Follow along to configure your system, install Ruby using the RubyInstaller, manage gems, create your first Rails project, and launch the local server. This tutorial provides the foundation you need to start building powerful web applications with Rails on Windows.

summary:
## Installing Ruby on Rails on Windows 10
This guide outlines the necessary dependencies and steps to set up a Ruby on Rails development environment on a Windows 10 machine.

## Core Dependencies
Installing Rails requires several other software packages to be installed first.
- **Node.js**: For JavaScript runtime capabilities.
- **Yarn**: A package manager for JavaScript.
- **SQLite3**: The default database for new Rails applications.

### 1. Install Node.js
- Download the **LTS (Long-Term Support)** version from the official [Node.js website](https://nodejs.org/).
- Run the installer with the default options.
- Verify the installation by running the following command in your terminal:
  > `node --version`

### 2. Install Yarn
- Once Node.js is installed, you have access to `npm` (Node Package Manager).
- **Method 1 (Recommended):** Use npm to install Yarn globally.
  > `npm install --global yarn`
- **Method 2:** Download the `.msi` installer from the [Yarn website](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install#windows-stable) for the stable version.
- Verify the installation:
  > `yarn --version`

### 3. Set up SQLite3
> [!IMPORTANT]
> This step is crucial for the default Rails database to work on Windows.

- Go to the [SQLite download page](https://www.sqlite.org/download.html).
- Navigate to the "Precompiled Binaries for Windows" section.
- Download two sets of files for your system's architecture (e.g., 64-bit):
  1. The `sqlite-dll` zip archive (contains 2 files).
  2. The `sqlite-tools` zip archive (contains 3 files).
- Extract all **five** files and copy them into your `C:\Windows\System32` directory.
- Verify the installation:
  > `sqlite3 --version`

## Installing Ruby and Rails
### 1. Install Ruby
- Download and run the **RubyInstaller** from the [official website](https://rubyinstaller.org/).
- Choose the latest recommended version.
- The installer will also set up `gem`, the Ruby package manager.
- Verify both installations:
  > `ruby --version`
  > `gem --version`

### 2. Install the Rails and SQLite3 Gems
- Use `gem` to install the necessary packages from your command prompt.
- First, install the SQLite3 adapter for Ruby:
  > `gem install sqlite3`
- Next, install Rails itself. This may take a few minutes.
  > `gem install rails`
- Verify the Rails installation:
  > `rails --version`

## Creating and Running Your First App
### 1. Generate a New Project
- Navigate to the directory where you want to create your project (e.g., your Desktop).
- Run the `rails new` command followed by your project's name:
  > `rails new my_project`
- Rails will create a new directory and install all the required gems for the project using Bundler.

### 2. Run the Rails Server
- Change into your new project's directory:
  > `cd my_project`
- Start the Puma web server:
  > `rails server`
- Open your web browser and navigate to **http://localhost:3000** to see your new Rails application running.

## Quick Overview: Rails MVC Architecture
Rails follows the **Model-View-Controller (MVC)** design pattern.
- **Model**: Manages data and business logic, interacting with the database.
- **View**: Handles the presentation layer—the front-end UI that the user sees.
- **Controller**: Manages application logic and communication, linking the Model and the View.
